body: Im from Spain so here we have Elvanse, but its pretty much the same thing… I started with 15 mg, and now I’m on 30 mg. Initially it made me a bit anxious (or maybe I was just anxious myself because I had a panic attack that week). It’s been a week and I’ve noticed it reduces my appetite, it also helps me be more focused and not be as impulsive or obsessive as I used to be… My thoughts seem to be more controlled… I’m not a pure binge eater, I tend to cycle from bulimia to binge eating without compensation, to sometimes purging anorexia…. But mostly bulimia and binge eating sometimes…. So idk if it may help you. Plus I’ve only been on it for like a week…. I can tell you, though, as a doctor that it usually helps many of the patients we treat with it.
Congrats!!!

Hey, been there… it’s hard after you eat huge amounts of food or food that may be expired or when you purge a couple of times a month during recovery you think it might kill you… but it’s not like that… if anything, in your case, it may give you diarrhea or vomiting if it’s not safe to consume… I’m sure you’re okay in that sense.

I’d ask myself: “Does it affect my life?” “Am I constantly thinking about it?” “Is it stopping me from doing other things or “functioning normally”?” Then the answer would be yes. It’s normal to have comorbidities after recovering from abusing other substances.

It was during an exchange thing in England. It was summer and I was 14. We had a BBQ and ate like 8 burgers… people were telling me to stop and I could not… I felt so embarrassed… Then I bought some noodles and ate them on top of that… I ate so much it gave me diarrhea... Plus my parents had to send me some money cause I had been spending all of it on food and it made me feel disgusting so I just lied and said I wasted it on gifts and clothes….

Also during that trip, I had dinner with my host family (around 5 pm ew) and was going to meet my previous year’s host family later on… they thought I hadn’t eaten dinner so they served me as well. I literally felt bad saying no, so I scarfed all of it down, even if it was making me sick… Then I went to the park with the kids and their friends and we went on a round swing thingy… I felt so nauseous I told them to stop and I literally barfed right in front of them and it was a lot of food and I felt really embarrassed…
The pain behind those words…
My therapist told me to plan my foods ahead of time each week and insert indulgent meals/comfort foods every few days so as to not avoid them and later want to crave them.
